faq.q: What is the difference between a formal and an informal letter?
faq.a: An informal letter goes to someone you know well and sounds chatty. A formal letter goes to an organisation or official, uses polite full words and follows a set layout.

faq.q: How do I end a formal letter?
faq.a: If you began Dear Sir or Madam, end with Yours faithfully. If you began with their name, like Dear Mr Tanaka, end with Yours sincerely. Then sign your full name.

faq.q: Where does the address go in a letter?
faq.a: In a British-style formal letter your address goes at the top right, with the date underneath, and the person's address on the left. Many modern and emailed letters put everything on the left.

faq.q: Can I use contractions in a formal letter?
faq.a: It is better not to. Write I am instead of I'm, and do not instead of don't, to sound polite and serious.
asks: I'm or I am in a formal letter?

faq.q: What goes in the paragraphs of a formal letter?
faq.a: First say why you are writing. Next give the details or reasons. Finally say clearly what you would like to happen.

facts: In British formal letters, Yours faithfully follows Dear Sir or Madam, and Yours sincerely follows a named greeting.
Many countries, including the USA, more often put everything on the left of a formal letter, called block style.
